scenes.title: A stone dropped from rest
scenes.source: f150–f179; requested dropped variant of 15 m diagram

beats.text: Consider a stone released from rest. It falls faster and faster. Find its velocity before impact.
It falls fifteen metres: displacement minus fifteen metres.
Initial velocity is zero; acceleration, minus ten. Ignore air resistance.
Let us calculate. Final velocity squared equals initial velocity squared plus twice acceleration times displacement.
beats.caption: Use the equation without time

beats.text: Zero squared, plus two times minus ten, times minus fifteen.
Velocity squared is three hundred. Which sign for velocity?
Minus seventeen point three metres per second. Negative means downward velocity before impact.
Thrown down instead? Initial velocity would be negative.
beats.caption: Thrown down: initial velocity is negative

scenes.title: Returning to the launch height

beats.text: Picture a ball thrown up at twelve metres per second, and caught back at the same height it left. No air resistance. Up is positive.
Acceleration is minus ten metres per second squared. Find velocity on return.
Final velocity squared equals initial velocity squared plus twice acceleration times displacement.
Twelve squared, plus two times minus ten times zero. S is zero because it is back where it started.
So v squared equals u squared: one hundred and forty four.
Taking square roots gives v equals plus or minus twelve.
It is coming down, so velocity is minus twelve metres per second. Same speed, opposite direction.
beats.caption: Same speed, opposite direction

beats.text: Now the velocity time graph. These equal triangles have opposite signed areas. The total displacement is zero.
beats.caption: Equal areas; zero total displacement

beats.text: This only works if it lands at the same height with no air resistance. Thrown from a cliff, it lands faster.
beats.caption: Same height, no air resistance

scenes.title: A stone thrown from a cliff

beats.text: Consider a stone thrown up from a cliff. It rises, returns past the edge, then hits the sea. Find its total flight time.
It leaves at eight metres per second upward.
The cliff is twenty metres high: displacement to sea, minus twenty metres.
Freely under gravity, acceleration is minus ten; upward positive.

scenes.title: Time until the stone reaches the sea

beats.text: Find the unknown time. Start with the displacement equation.
beats.caption: Find the total time of flight

beats.text: Displacement equals initial velocity times time, plus half acceleration times time squared.
Minus twenty equals eight t, plus half times minus ten t squared.
Rearrange: five t squared minus eight t minus twenty equals zero.
Solving this quadratic gives minus one point three five four, or two point nine five four seconds.
Reject the negative root: before projection. Time must be positive.
The total time of flight is two point nine five seconds, to three significant figures.
This includes the extra fall below the cliff edge.
beats.caption: Total flight includes the fall below launch

scenes.title: Maximum height above the sea

beats.text: Find maximum height above sea. First, the rise above the cliff.
beats.caption: Find the height above the sea

beats.text: At the top, velocity is zero. Initial velocity eight; acceleration minus ten.
Final velocity squared equals initial velocity squared plus twice acceleration times displacement.
Zero squared equals eight squared plus two times minus ten times s.
So zero equals sixty four minus twenty s.
The rise is three point two metres above the launch point.
Height above sea equals cliff height plus rise.
beats.caption: Add the cliff height

beats.text: Twenty plus three point two gives twenty three point two metres above the sea.
